items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: Now he was a player in the band years before that. I’m very fond of his playing. He comes to a lot of these parties.

ctx.x: So you saw them in Condon’s club? Was it Eddie Condon’s?

Yes. 47 West Third Street it was at first then they later moved to a club up on First Avenue and 40th Street or something like that, and then finally down next to where Jimmy Ryan’s was on 24th Street near the Sheraton Hotel. And by that time of course Ed Polcer became the manager. Now he was a player in the band years before that. I’m very fond of his playing. He comes to a lot of these parties. And he’s also graduated in © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

business from Cornell or someplace like that. He’s a very bright person and a fine guy. They’ve all, those people have been so good to me that I just can’t believe it. But there’s nothing that I can give to them except friendship and they think they’re sympathetic that I like what they’re doing. They appreciate that.
